title: 3D outgoing Helmholtz Green function selected by the Sommerfeld radiation condition
expression_sketch: R = sqrt((x - x0)**2 + (y - y0)**2 + (z - z0)**2); u_plus = exp(I*k*R)/(4*pi*R); u_minus = exp(-I*k*R)/(4*pi*R); general combination u = c*u_plus + (1 - c)*u_minus. Only u_plus satisfies Sommerfeld: limit(|x|->oo, |x|**((n-1)/2)*(diff(u, |x|) - I*k*u)) = 0 for time-harmonic convention exp(-I*omega*t), n = 3, k > 0.
latent_structure: Two specializations of the spherical-wave master exp(s*k*R)/(4*pi*R) with s = +/- I. Sommerfeld radiation (outgoing vs incoming) selects one member of the family. The singularity at R = 0 is the source point, not a CSE of the denominator.

function_domains.u: radiating solution of Helmholtz on R^n, n in {2, 3}

nonzero_conditions.statement: Classical pointwise formula is written with |x - x0| in the denominator (R != 0)
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Wikipedia Sommerfeld radiation condition: u_pm(x) = exp(+/- i k |x-x0|)/(4*pi*|x-x0|)

positivity_conditions.label: DECLARED
positivity_conditions.source: Wikipedia Sommerfeld radiation condition: 'k > 0 is a constant, called the wave number'

analytic_domains.statement: Inhomogeneous Helmholtz (nabla^2 + k^2) u = -f in R^n for n = 2, 3, with f of compact support
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED

analytic_domains.statement: Radiating solutions satisfy the Sommerfeld radiation condition uniformly in direction x/|x|
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Wikipedia Sommerfeld radiation condition: lim_{|x|->oo} |x|^{(n-1)/2} (d/d|x| - i k) u(x) = 0

analytic_domains.statement: Time-harmonic convention is exp(-i omega t); the opposite convention replaces -i by +i in Sommerfeld
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Wikipedia Sommerfeld radiation condition, Formulation, last paragraph

analytic_domains.statement: Of the family u = c u_+ + (1-c) u_-, only u_+ is radiating for the stated Sommerfeld sign
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Wikipedia Sommerfeld radiation condition: 'Of all these solutions, only u_+ satisfies the Sommerfeld radiation condition'

branch_conventions: |x - x0| is the Euclidean distance (nonnegative square root).
Outgoing spherical wave is exp(+i k R) for the exp(-i omega t) convention.

limit_domains.statement: |x| -> infinity uniformly in all directions, with the Sommerfeld operator (d/d|x| - i k)
limit_domains.label: DECLARED
limit_domains.source: Wikipedia Sommerfeld radiation condition: limit as |x| -> oo uniformly in direction

source_provenance: Sommerfeld, A., Partial Differential Equations in Physics, Academic Press, 1949
Jackson, J. D., Classical Electrodynamics, outgoing Helmholtz Green function G_k = exp(i k |x-x'|)/(4*pi*|x-x'|)

public_source: Wikipedia, Sommerfeld radiation condition (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sommerfeld_radiation_condition); Sommerfeld, Partial Differential Equations in Physics (1949).
why_not_cse_lgg: CSE shares |x-x0| in the two spherical waves. LGG antiunifies exp(+/- i k R)/R as a first-order template with a sign hole. The scientific representation is radiation selection of one member of a two-point family, not a common subexpression.
proposer_leak_risk: Do not plant sealed-control gold names. 'Sommerfeld', 'outgoing', and 'Hankel' should not appear as gold target wording in a later proposer view.
notes: Normalization follows the cited Sommerfeld Wikipedia page (no overall minus). Jackson's (nabla^2 + k^2) G = -delta uses G = exp(i k R)/(4*pi*R). Limiting absorption Im k > 0 is not used: it is not written on the cited page and is not inserted. Real k > 0 plus Sommerfeld is the declared uniqueness condition. Not the sealed G3 control.
